body: viola verify output: the step lines a live verify --record prints while it records the set, and the interrupted-verify exit and stderr pair if a live run is cut short.

Recorder hygiene through the scrub: no host path, user name, email, token or status-line text in any recorded file; a payload holding a home path is refused, never scrubbed by hand; paths are not carried into output.
The home a live verify --record takes comes from a record-home helper and holds no path component named home, so the recorder never refuses its own payloads.
Vendor content stays behind the single vendor-content boundary: the recorded screens and payloads are claude's content, read only by signatures, never parsed beyond them; kept screens stay local.

The placeholder hint read as box-text holds-text: whether the screen model can tell it apart from typed text by a cell attribute is measured, without widening screen-content parsing beyond signatures.
Boundary and drift tests sequenced on the recorded records: the fake agent replays the new set in CI, and the readings it gates on come from records, never from a live run.
Live readings never gate: the live starts (the verify --record, the tap re-record, the StopFailure capture, the /context send) are evidence for the record, not a CI check.

The StopFailure payload's error word read against the cause map: a word of the CLI's set yields its cause, and no unlisted code word is dropped or parse-rejected silently; code words keep their kebab-case format.
The human keeps the wheel at the TUI boundary during live starts: viola never answers or seeds the CLI's browser-tools prompt; a person answers it once on the host.
Time bounds fall on the driver only: any wait or dialog hold a live start or replay uses bounds the driver, never the human.
The remove-the-guard control runs on a filtered test entry (a case filter or no fail-fast) so the named case is read red; the CI gate itself stays fail-fast with no skips and no retries.
The 24 relied ledger rows read STAMPED against the new set; a stamp written before the newer rows reads unverified until verify runs again.

pause and release, the driver-originated release guard and its contracts: untouched.
The Hyprland recorder, its reply-text drop and the hyprctl deadline: no window-manager reading is recorded here.
config.json keys and their bad-value handling: no configuration key is added or read anew.
Release, signing and deploy rows, release-check output and attested release builds: the chunk ships no release.
The board scan and viola list's home read rule and colour facts: untouched.
The CLI exit-code table, the --json error documents and the instance-unreachable detail causes: no CLI verb's output changes.

**2026-09-24-fake-agent-and-test-data-fixtures** (fixture naming and the `--fixtures` root) — fixtures named `<Event>.<variant>.json` by the CLI's own PascalCase hook name with no mapping table, the fake agent joining `<cli-version>` under the parent `--fixtures fixtures/claude`; a payload replayed as recorded bytes, consumer-first, no shape invented before a recorded fixture. The new `fixtures/claude/2.1.325/` set must land in this exact layout (decision/fixture-named-by-hook-event, contract/claude-fixtures/payload-path).

**2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify** — the fixture hygiene walk is a run-time directory walk over `fixtures/claude/*/*.json`, not rstest `#[files]`, because rstest 0.27 refuses an empty glob at compile time. A new version dir joins the walk with no code edit, and every file in it must pass schema and the unclean checks (decision/fixture-hygiene-walk).

**2026-09-29-verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness** — `stamped_home` and `Wrapper::boot` pin `--cli-version` to the recorded set's version; the fake agent's `DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION` equals that version and the harness `boot --cli-version` default matches (decision/harness-cli-version-matches-fake). It also specified `run --local-live` (suite `local-live`, `row-missing` / `verify-exit-<n>` codes, `live-in-ci` refusal under `CI`). If this chunk moves the default to 2.1.325, every one of these sites moves together.

**2026-09-29-fake-agent-drift-contract** — `contract_fake_agent_drift` compares the fake agent's hook stdin byte for byte with each recorded `fixtures/claude/<ver>/` set, walked at run time, an empty walk failing; never insta (insta is kept for decision bodies only). The 2.1.325 set is replayed by this walk automatically, so every variant it records must replay byte-exact (decision/fake-agent-contract-suite, decision/fixture-drift-byte-compare, decision/fake-transcripts-compared-to-recordings).

**2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id** — the precedent for moving the default CLI version (2.1.283 → 2.1.287 across `DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION`, `RECORDED_CLI_VERSION`, `stamped_home`, `Wrapper::boot`) and for the hygiene walk naming the sets it covers. The relayed dialog tier it describes was later superseded by recordings. This is the checklist if 2.1.325 becomes the default.

**2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes** — `contract_ledger_probes` keeps literal lists: stamped sets and drift-only sets, every fixture dir on exactly one list; screens are a separate fixture class checked against `schemas/claude-screen.v1.json`, signature rows only, scrub-as-detector, refused whole. A new `2.1.325` dir must be put on one list (the scope's «`STAMPED`»), or the census fails (decision/ledger-probe-contract-suite, decision/screen-fixture-scrub-as-detector).

A set without them is run without `--framing` and must exit 1, and only the stamped set(s) end `N pass  0 fail`, the others staying drift-only. A partial 2.1.325 set cannot be listed `STAMPED`.

A route entry's live readings are a local measurement, not a suite.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (`viola verify`'s refusal codes) — verify writes its refusal code on `process-exit` under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`. A recording refused as unclean is `Ended::Refused` with `detail` `unclean-fixture`, and the fixture's file name enters no code. A failing row is no refusal and carries no code, and verify takes no `--json`. A dirty 2.1.325 recording surfaces this way (contract/verify-exit-detail/unclean-fixture, decision/verify-failing-row-no-refusal, decision/verify-takes-no-json).

body: The recorded fixture set per CLI version: a new 2.1.325 set beside 2.1.283, 2.1.287, 2.1.288 and 2.1.302, produced only by a live verify recording and landed whole, never hand-written or hand-edited.
Recording only at zero failing rows: the live verify that records the set must read every relied ledger row passing (24 relied rows), or the recording is refused.

Recorder hygiene through the recorder's scrub: no host path, user name, email, token or status-line text in any recorded file; a dirty payload refuses the recording whole and is never scrubbed by hand; screens kept by the run stay local.

Record homes never named home: the live rig's record home comes from a helper like the tests' record home helper and holds no path component named home, since a recorder refuses a payload holding /home/.

The MCP exchange recorded by the test-only tap, which refuses a dirty exchange whole; the re-recorded tools/list reads the list tool's description without the usage-budget wording, and the tool set the server advertises is what the recording holds.

The fake agent replays recorded bytes for the new version, and its transcripts are compared byte for byte against the recordings: the drift suites and every-version replay must run over 2.1.325 in CI.
Recorded fixtures checked against their tolerant schema and named by hook event, at the recorded payload path the fixture contract names; the run-time fixture hygiene walk reaches the new set.

The ledger probes' stamped reading: viola verify's stamped line and summary read against the new set, every ledger row with its verify probe, the version gate needing every relied row, and stamps written only by verify.

The StopFailure hook, registered with no ledger row and no verify probe: a live StopFailure payload recorded inside a started session's turn, its error word read against the nine-word cause map with no parse-rejected unknown-value line for any of the CLI's 13 words; the exception settled as a ledger row with its probe or kept on the founder's word.
The 22nd relied row local-command-echo leaves every earlier stamp unverified until verify runs again: the re-stamp is live, under the founder's cap word.

Local commands confirmed by their post-condition only: /context's post-condition measured live, and whether /mcp disable of an absent server writes to the user's real Claude config; a local command with no measured post-condition stays unconfirmable.

The screen read only for compiled signatures: the box text holds-text reading, provisionally the CLI's placeholder hint, measured for whether a cell attribute the screen model reads tells the hint apart from typed text; the rendered child screen is never parsed beyond that.

The browser-tools prompt: viola never answers or seeds it; on a host where it was never answered a real verify reads 8 of 24 and the version stays unverified; whether viola ever answers or seeds it is left to the founder.
Run E's resume start: the clean recording records Run E, so its record reads whether Run E starts on a SessionStart capture the resume target accepts.

The bounded remove-the-guard witness for the browser-tools row: the bt-absent control fired on a filtered run (a case filter or no fail-fast) so the named case that verifies the absent browser-tools row is counted is read red without the guard.

Real claude only locally, never in CI: every live start runs on the local host through the local-live path, names the 2.1.325 install by its path rather than a bare claude, and each start's count needs the founder's cap word.
A live reading is recorded as read, never as verification: nothing is claimed for 2.1.326 or 2.1.327, and readings made under the rig's private config are not claimed for the live home.
The pinned product binary that drives the builder is not rebuilt or re-pinned before or by this chunk's verify; a binary built from the tree reads earlier 22- or 23-row stamps unverified.
Each of the entry's carries is disposed by name, none dropped or widened; no mutation run and no scheduled wake or timer belong to this chunk.
